How configurations are selected 1. Sources are collected from curated public repositories and Iran-focused collectors. 2. Invalid, duplicate and insecure entries are removed (for example VLESS without TLS). 3. Each configuration is scored on protocol, transport, security, port, SNI / Host and CDN fronting. 4. Candidates are tested for TCP reachability, then TLS and WebSocket handshake, then an end-to-end proxy request where the protocol allows. 5. Final lists are built tier by tier, with limits per port, host and subnet.
Important notes - Checks run from outside Iran. They confirm that a server is alive and proxies traffic, but they cannot guarantee access from every ISP or on every day. - Filtering conditions change often. If one configuration stops working, try another one or refresh the subscription. - Public configurations are shared infrastructure. Avoid sensitive activity on them. - Provided for educational and research purposes. Use responsibly and in accordance with local laws.
